card.name: Berd
card.era: Origins in historic Vaspurakan; medieval roots
card.tagline: The 'fortress' dance where men build a human tower
card.profile: Berd (Բերդ, also Berdapar), meaning "fortress," is an Armenian military folk dance famous for a circle of men standing on the shoulders of another circle to create a rotating human tower (Armenian dance, Wikipedia; NaTakallam). It originates from the old Armenian region of Vaspurakan near Lake Van in Western Armenia, and is said to derive from a game called gmbetakhagh ("dome game"). Performed by men to drum and zurna, it dramatizes the storming and defense of a fortress.
card.insight: Berd vividly literalizes the idea of collective strength: by physically constructing a "fortress" from interlocked bodies, the dance enacts community defense and unity, themes deeply tied to Armenian highland history (NaTakallam).
